entities.name: Marcus Geganius Macerinus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Marcus Geganius Macerinus was a Roman statesman of immense influence in the 5th century BCE, serving as Consul in 447, 443, and 437 BC, and as Censor in 435 BC.

As a key figure in the Roman Republic, he played a crucial role in shaping the country's governance and politics. His leadership and vision helped establish the foundations for the Roman Empire's expansion and dominance in the Mediterranean region.

Macerinus's legacy extends beyond his own time, as he was succeeded by notable Roman leaders such as Appius Claudius Caecus and Scipio Africanus.

The inscription on his tomb, now lost, is said to have read, 'Marcus Geganius Macerinus, son of Marcus, Consul for the third time, and Censor,' a testament to his esteemed status within Roman society.
